sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Certified Good Distribution Practice (GDP) Clinical Logistics

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with commercial, maritime and private foundation law influenced by international practice)

Panama–Spain General Agreement on Economic Cooperation
Panama–United Arab Emirates Bilateral Investment Treaty

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin / Passport-issuing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature; Hague Apostille if bank is abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the Founder, all Foundation Council members, Protector, and all Ultimate Beneficial Owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Panama's UAF national sanctions and terrorism lists, and Panama's PEP database. Foreign PEPs automatically require enhanced due diligence irrespective of the Low_Risk business tier; domestic PEPs require escalated approval where public procurement or government contracting risk is identified. Screening must be completed within five business days prior to registration and evidence retained for at least five years after dissolution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) — online corporate name search and reservation via the official portal www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed foundation name must be filed in Spanish transliteration or in a Latin-script form acceptable to the Public Registry. Names may be in any language using Latin characters, but the Registry may require a Spanish-language translation of the name. The name must include the term 'Foundation' or 'Fundación' or a permitted abbreviation, and must not be identical, deceptively similar, or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of name rejection, the applicant or legal counsel may file a written reconsideration appeal with the Dirección General de Registro of the Public Registry of Panama within ten business days of the rejection notice, pursuant to the Registry Regulation and applicable administrative procedure rules. The appeal must include a legal memorandum demonstrating that the proposed name is not prohibited, does not infringe any third-party trademark, and is not misleading or contrary to public order. The Registry must issue a decision within fifteen business days. If the appeal is denied, counsel may file a further judicial appeal before the Administrative Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, or submit an alternative name reselection without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for administrative correspondence and statutory registered-office purposes for a Private Interest Foundation; however, for the ISIC 5229 GDP Pharma Freight commercial license, the licensing authorities — including the Ministry of Health (MINSA) and the National Directorate of Pharmacy and Drugs — require a demonstrable physical operating address where GDP-compliant temperature-controlled handling, quarantine storage, and supervisory oversight may be verified. A purely digital/virtual address will not satisfy the commercial substance requirements for the pharma freight operating license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high probability, quantified as approximately 35% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months of GDP license qualification and approximately 65% probability once the Ministry of Health initiates good-distribution-practice certification inspections. Pre-incorporation inspections are rare unless the prior business reputation of the applicant triggers enhanced regulatory vetting.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995) on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law No. 53 of 2001 and Law No. 13 of 9 April 2015; applicable sections on foundation charter execution, endowment, registered agent, and the Foundation Council (Consejo de la Fundación).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fondaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Foundations Department), with the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) subsequently administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter), executed by private document or public deed and filed for inscription with the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The foundation endowment must be at least US$10,000 (or assets of equivalent market value); no full cash escrow is mandated at formation—the Foundation Council may evidence the endowment by declaration in the charter or by a subsequent contribution protocol, subject to the Public Registry's minimum capitalization verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF PA_PIF (PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION): 1. The Charter inscribed under Law 25 of 1995 is adopted, and the initial endowment of US$10,000 is accepted as the foundation patrimony. 2. The registered office is fixed at the address of the Resident Agent in the Republic of Panama. 3. Founding Council members are ratified, and the Protector is confirmed as designated in the Charter. 4. The Council delegates ordinary administration of GDP-compliant pharmaceutical freight operations to the appointed Administrator, and authorizes the opening of bank accounts, execution of customs and logistics contracts, and retention of the Sanitary License.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entity Name Clearance and Charter Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certificado de Aviso / Name Approval Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance request for 'PA_PIF Private Interest Foundation' (or authorized Spanish equivalent containing the term 'Fundación de Interés Privado'); upon a roll of the registry deposit drawer, obtain certification of non-identical-name, then instruct a Panamanian attorney to draft the Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) with council composition, endowment clauses, and contemplated GDP pharma freight activity.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of applicant identification and statutory representation powers
Power of attorney to the founding attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of rejection for name similarity, promptly file an opposition brief or amend the proposed corporate designation and repay the aviso tariff within the statutory term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the founders execute the Acta de Fundación either in private form before the Resident Agent, or as public deed before a licensed notary; ensure stipulation of the initial US$10,000 endowment, registered office, Foundation Council members, Protector (optional), and the authorized ISIC 5229 logistics commercial scope.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of founder(s) and council members
Notarial protocol for public deed version
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any notarial defect by marginal amendment annotation in the protocol and re-execute the affected sheet before further registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Filing and Legalization at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fondaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the executed Foundation Charter to the Foundations Department together with the official fee deposit slip; the department verifies statutory minimum endowment, legality of clauses under Law 25/1995 and Law 13/2015, and interior legality of the commercial-objective provisions related to transportation support services.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for the filing counsel
Resident Agent declaration and registered-office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Honor the Department's 'notas de defecto' (deficiency notes) by submitting supplementary clarifications or amended pages within the legal window; renewed registration follows upon full cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Tax Identifier Procurement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, online via Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) application using the registered foundation data, obtain the estándar commercial-activities tax classification, and register presumed income treatment for foreign-source assets while confirming local-source territorial scope on logistics activities; issue the foundational electronic certificate.
required_dossiers: Public Registry inscription certificate of the foundation
Registered-office lease agreement or registered agent certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a declaratory rectification before the DGI if the RUC classification, activity codes, or territorial-presumption flags are incorrectly assigned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Departamento de Rentas Municipales / Sertracen e-Tramita Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal Aviso de Operación for the logistics/transportation-support activity, declare warehouse premises, pay the annual municipal rate, and post the permit at the registered physical headquarters before commercial activation.
required_dossiers: Public Registry certificate of the foundation
Lease contract or property title of the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal office objects for zoning inconsistency,  update the lease documents or request an exceptional use variance from the Municipality's Zoning Directorate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Statutory Books and Foundation Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent Office and Foundation Council Internal Procedure (via registered protocol)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the Foundation Council minute book and foundation asset register, record the sworn acceptance of council members, execute the standard first-board minutes approving the 80-120 word First Resolution adopted by the Council, and maintain the beneficial-ownership register in accordance with Anti-Money-Laundering regulations of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and Superintendencia de Bancos protocol for low-risk non-deposit foundation structures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate missing statutory books by having the Public Registry authorize a late book-law-notarization and correct any retrospective filing in the register book rubric.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) — Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas in coordination with the Autoridad Panameña de Seguridad de Alimentos (AUPSA) only where food-adjacent pharmaceutical freight occurs; freight-side land operation governed by Dirección Nacional de Transporte.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Sanitaria de Funcionamiento para Almacén de Distribución Farmacéutica (Good Distribution Practice — GDP Warehouse Operating License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría II — Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Específico (EsIA Específico) for pharmaceutical freight logistics storing temperature-controlled goods with refrigerated equipment and delivery vehicle fleets; registration-level (Categoría I) pathway available if site operations are limited exclusively to contamination-free dry warehousing below 1,500 m2 with no cold-chain discharge units.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0112-2010 effluent-discharge rules (pH 6.0-9.0, TSS, BOD5 thresholds) for any sanitary or condensate discharges; VOCs: application of Recovery/Leak-Detection Protocol for refrigerant gases under Executive Decree 1235 of 2014 and Montreal Protocol schedules; cold-chain equipment must maintain FDA/WHO GDP temperature-mapping of 2-8°C or 15-25°C envelopes without CFC emissive refrigerants; waste: segregated disposal registry that meets Panamanian hazardous-waste manifest rules and WHO/PQS pharmaceutical waste standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification (Visto Bueno) issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá after technical inspection of the warehouse egress, suppression systems, and emergency illumination, plus the Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil (SINAPROC) disaster-response alignment certificate; structural load inspection certification of racking and mezzanine systems by a licensed engineer; occupational health clearance for warehouse personnel issued by the Comisión de Salud Ocupacional (General Directorate of Occupational Health) of MINSA and a workplace-risk assessment protocol under the MITRADEL Hygiene and Safety regulations, together with the mandatory biosecurity protocol for pharmaceutical cargo handlers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); e-portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa; export and customs supervision by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident founders must appoint a resident agent (agente residente), then register the Private Interest Foundation (Fundación de Interés Privado) charter with the Registro Público de Panamá to obtain the ficha (foundation file number). Thereafter: obtain a municipal Aviso de Operación; file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application with DGI via its portal or local office, presenting the certified foundation charter, ficha, resident agent credentials, registered office confirmation, and identification of the foundation council. The RUC serves as the single TIN/VAT ID. The PIF must then register as an ITBMS collector, select the invoicing modality (electronic invoicing or authorized fiscal printer), and complete the annual Aviso de Operación renewal. No separate NIT exists beyond the RUC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box regime. A PIF is a separate juridical person taxed territorially: only Panama-source income is subject to income tax. The foundation may elect in its charter to adopt corporate-style governance; it may elect to register with DGI for Panama-source logistics/invoicing activities and, where average monthly gross sales do not exceed USD 3,000 (annualized USD 36,000), may elect the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS quota regime. No pass-through or hybrid-mismatch elections exist under Panamanian law; territorial source attribution follows the Fiscal Code, principally Article 699.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) - VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold: any person performing taxable supplies in Panama must obtain RUC and register for ITBMS. A simplified small-taxpayer quota regime (Régimen Especial Simplificado) applies to businesses with average monthly gross turnover not exceeding USD 3,000 (annual maximum of USD 36,000). GDP pharma freight operators are expected to register under the general regime because of export documentation and refund mechanics.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama is progressively mandating electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) through DGI-authorized e-invoicing platforms or the DGI online system. Invoices must be transmitted to DGI, digitally signed, and carry a unique DGI authorization code and QR/validation stamp; authorized fiscal printers remain transitional for qualifying small taxpayers. Zero-rated export freight invoices must identify the GDP shipment, the client's foreign or Panamanian tax identifier, and the applicable 0% export code, and must be issued through the approved ITBMS invoicing channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating (0% ITBMS) is available for: (i) physical export of goods to a non-resident consignee where the goods leave Panama; (ii) international transport of cargo, including freight forwarding, customs brokerage, and ancillary logistics services directly connected with the export operation; and (iii) services rendered to persons residing abroad whose benefit is realized entirely outside Panama. The GDP pharma freight operator must hold a valid RUC/exporter registration, issue zero-rated invoices, and prove that the cargo physically departed its Panama facility. Panama-to-Panama transport legs and pre-export warehousing remain subject to 7% unless directly and exclusively linked to an export transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) validated by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/bank transfer proof of foreign currency settlement
Zero-rated export invoice and underlying commercial invoice with GDP cargo description
GDP temperature excursion/transport protocol records evidencing cargo integrity
Exporter registry certificate (Registro de Exportadores), pharma license, and GDP accreditation certificate where required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may retroactively revoke zero-rated status where the export documentation bundle is incomplete, inconsistent, or untimely, reassessing ITBMS at 7% with statutory interest, surcharges, and administrative fines. The clawback limitation period is five years, extended to ten years in cases of fraud, concealment, or omission. Wilful false export declarations constitute tax fraud, exposing the PIF, its foundation council, resident agent, and signatories to criminal prosecution under Panama's Penal Code, fines, registry suspension, customs penalties under Panama's customs legislation, and exclusion from the exporter registry.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank; the foreign exchange and banking regime is administered by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks), with Banco Nacional de Panamá acting as fiscal agent and the Ministry of Economy and Finance supervising monetary and exchange matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions. The US dollar is legal tender under Decree Law 20 of 1904; there is no exchange control, no mandatory central bank approval, and no restriction on the repatriation of profits, dividends, or capital. Profit remittance is subject only to corporate tax and any applicable dividend distribution taxes under the territorial tax regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender and no mandatory conversion ratio exists. Export receipts may be retained in USD or any freely traded currency, credited to any Panamanian banking institution, and disbursed without exchange control consent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational corporate account for freight disbursements and trade settlements
Capital escrow account and government-linked transaction account
Both capital escrow and operational account for cross-border pharma logistics

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability until a full Panamanian banking license is obtained. Panama does not issue a dedicated EMI license; digital banks and fintech platforms must operate through a licensed Panamanian bank or hold a foreign license, which is generally not accepted for direct clearing. Offshore EMI accounts may be used for ancillary payment collection but are not viable as primary treasury rails for GDP pharma freight settlement without a Panamanian license and local compliance seat.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively required for directors or authorized officers for the initial account opening of a non-resident-controlled Private Interest Foundation. Remote opening is available only for existing clients or with a legally appointed representative holding a notarized power of attorney; most tier-1 banks require at least one signatory to appear physically before the compliance officer or a notarized interview with a recognized Panamanian attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation lacking clear commercial substance and identifiable ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation charter, notarized board resolution, registered agent certificate, complete UBO identification with passport copies, proof of the foundation's seat and purpose, and a business plan demonstrating active GDP pharma freight operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk pharma freight activity flagged due to controlled cargo and public health supply chain commodities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the Ministerio de Salud pharmaceutical logistics or wholesale license, Good Distribution Practice (GDP) certificate, freight forwarding license issued by the Panama Maritime Authority or relevant transport authority, signed client and supplier agreements, and customs broker credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth concerns for inbound capital injections from non-resident founders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements, tax filings, bank reference letters from the source jurisdiction, purchase contracts and pro-forma invoices evidencing commercial rationale, and a detailed funding schedule showing the provenance of every inward transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows to embargoed or high-risk jurisdictions in the pharmaceutical supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening clearance reports, end-user certificates, export license for controlled medicinal goods, cargo manifests, and a standardized counterparty due-diligence file for each beneficiary including ultimate beneficial owner documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be executed through SWIFT wire transfers using MT103 or MT202 messages, citing the true economic purpose such as 'capital contribution', 'foreign direct investment', 'parent company loan', or 'working capital advance for freight operations'. Panama applies no purpose-code system, but the bank's AML module will require a specific payment descriptor and supporting documentation; the foundation must retain a board resolution approving the injection and invoices or contracts evidencing the commercial transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for high-value international freight payments under the ISIC 5229 logistics model. Bank transfers must include the corresponding invoicing, CMR/airway bill or bill of lading, and cargo insurance certificate. Confirmed commercial letters of credit are recommended for the procurement of temperature-controlled pharmaceutical cargo and for settlement with non-established suppliers; local disbursements within Panama may be executed through Direct ACH using the Cámara de Compensación Bancaria de Panamá.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign exchange contracts against USD for EUR, CHF, and other settlement currencies
Vanilla deliverable currency forwards for operational USD receivables and non-USD payables
Cross-currency basis swaps between USD and EUR/CHF for longer-term freight contracts
Interest-rate and cross-currency swaps on foundation treasury lines, subject to bank credit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Return/Payment (Tasa Única Anual) for Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 March; no extension or carry-forward available; calendar-year basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 5% of the fee, capped at 50%, plus 1% monthly interest; two consecutive unpaid years trigger administrative strike-off by DGI and the Registro Público; Foundation Council members may incur personal liability for continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Electronic Fiscal Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 April for the fiscal year ended 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to US$10,000 for inaccurate or incomplete filing; continued non-compliance blocks issuance of good-standing certificates, notarial acts, registry filings, and banking/license renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Good Standing Certificate (Certificado de Persona Jurídica) — evidence certificate for bank and license renewals; PIFs are exempt from filing annual financial statements with the Registro Público
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At any time after payment of the 15 March franchise tax; standard practice is to obtain by 30 April for MINSA GDP license and banking renewal packages
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not a statutory filing as such; issuance is refused until the franchise tax and UBO declaration are fully current, effectively suspending proof of corporate existence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Pharmaceutical GDP Logistics License (Renovación Anual de Licencia de Operador Logístico Farmacéutico / Habilitación Sanitaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) — Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas, in coordination with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas for freight validation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than 30 calendar days before the license anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers MINSA administrative fines and automatic suspension of GDP distribution and freight operations; continued non-renewal leads to revocation of the sanitary license and loss of customs brokerage eligibility.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A dormant or passive-asset PIF is not subject to a mandatory independent audit. Audit becomes compulsory when the foundation engages in commercial activity producing gross annual income exceeding US$3,000,000, when classified as a DGI large taxpayer under segmentation rules, or when the MINSA GDP license and customs freight validation regime expressly requires audited or reviewed financial statements certified by a Panamanian-licensed CPA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS and IFRS for SMEs as officially adopted by Panama; private interest foundations must maintain formal accounting records in accordance with Decree Law 34 of 1949 and DGI book-registration rules; entities below the audit threshold may apply IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 23 of 2015 as amended by Law 254 of 2021, the Foundation Council must declare all ultimate beneficial owners — including founders, council members, beneficiaries, and any person controlling foundation assets — in the annual DGI filing due by 30 April. Any shareholding or beneficial-interest transfer, foundation charter amendment, or change in beneficiaries must be reported to the registered agent and to DGI within 30 calendar days of the change. The registered agent must refresh identity, domicile, and source-of-funds evidence at each annual renewal and before processing any transaction exceeding US$10,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Foundation Charter, Founders and Beneficiaries Records)
Register of Directors (Foundation Council Members Register)
Minute Book (Foundation Council Resolutions and Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 850 – 1,500 per annum (registered agent, registered address, franchise-tax processing, and UBO declaration coordination)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 2,500 – 8,000 for a GDP-license review or compilation engagement; full IFRS audit US$ 8,000 – 15,000 if the US$3,000,000 revenue threshold or license conditions are triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% uniform CIT on Panama-source income; 5% surtax on taxable income exceeding USD 1.5M yields a 30% marginal rate for large taxpayers
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system: foreign-source freight, logistics and holding income of a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is outside the taxable base, resulting in 0% effective CIT; SEM (Multinational Headquarters) regime: 5% reduced rate or exemption for qualified regional service centers; CIT credit for reinvested profits in education (1.5% of payroll); capital gains from foreign asset sales are exempt for non-domiciled PIFs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 31 (Declaración de Renta – Personas Jurídicas); filed electronically via the SIE (Sistema de Información y Gestión Electrónica) portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); payments via SIE-integrated banking or Banco Nacional de Panamá
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; DGI assigns a staggered calendar by last RUC digit (typically extending to 15 April / 30 June for calendar-year taxpayers). A PIF with exclusively foreign-source income files no Form 31; the return becomes mandatory only when the PIF derives Panama-source commercial or logistics income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification: legal name, RUC, fiscal domicile, resident agent name and address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF must list the Panamanian Resident Agent's full data; the foundation's foreign address is acceptable as secondary reference

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic activity code (CIIU v4) and taxpayer regime
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510 (freight arrangement – GDP pharma) for the Panamanian logistics activity; identify regime as territorial

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue (ingresos brutos) attributable to Panama-source operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue from services executed in Panama or contracts sourced to Panama; foreign-source GDP freight revenue is declared as exempt in Line 1b

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt and foreign-source revenue (ingresos exentos y de fuente extranjera)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF managing international pharma GDP freight: report foreign-origin invoices here; attach a territoriality schedule showing execution abroad
Result of Line 1a minus Line 1b; if the PIF has no Panama-source activity, leave zero with supporting statement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attributable deductions: direct costs, cold-chain warehousing, insurance, transport, and professional fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses incurred to generate Panama-source income; allocate common costs using an arm's length apportionment method
Standard computation: Line 1c minus Line 1d; non-domiciled PIFs may leave zero
Apply 25% to Line 1e; no apportionment for foreign-source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 5% surtax on the portion of Line 1e exceeding USD 1.5M
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only for large taxpayers with Panama-source taxable income above the threshold

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings suffered, advance payments (anticipos), and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs claim back 12.5% or 10% Panamanian withholding credits only if they filed Form 31

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable or credit balance (saldo a favor)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Zero for purely foreign-source PIFs; payment due by the deadline; CPA signature required for gross revenue above USD 300,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% monthly surcharge on tax due, capped at 50%; default interest at 10% per annum (1.5% monthly civil surcharge) from the due date; failure to file despite a Panama-source activity triggers automatic assessment with a 10% fine and the loss of deduction rights; criminal exposure for willful non-filing under Código Penal Art. 288

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PIF Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única de Fundación de Interés Privado); payment authenticated via the RUC-calendared SIE payment slip (Voucher de Pago) and collectable through Banco Nacional or SIE electronic channels
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be settled within the first semester of each fiscal year, with the DGI calendar generally setting 30 June as the final payment date; the fee is obligatory regardless of income or activity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: USD 300 fixed annual tax when total foundational assets do not exceed USD 10,000 and no distributions were made
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident founders must ensure the Resident Agent pays through the RUC-linked PIF file to avoid registry suspension

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: USD 400 fixed annual tax when assets exceed USD 10,000 or any distribution to beneficiaries occurred during the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Resident Agent must retain the assets register and distribution minutes to justify the USD 400 tier in a DGI audit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Simplified statement that the foundation has no Panama-source income; must be retained in the statutory file
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF engages in GDP freight services physically in Panama, the statement is invalid and the PIF must file Form 31

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of the PIF annual fee: 5% monthly surcharge up to 50% and interest at 10% per annum; continuous non-payment causes the blocking of the foundation's good-standing certificate, the inability to open or maintain Panamanian bank accounts, and, following a two-year default, the foundation may be stricken from the Public Registry with asset-blocking consequences

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% complementary withholding on dividends paid out of Panama-source taxable profits of a commercial corporation or a PIF taxed as a corporation (combined effective burden: 25% CIT + 7.5% net dividend tax ≈ 32.5%); distributions by a PIF from foreign-source foundational assets are executed as gratuitous transfers and are subject to 0% Panamanian withholding; a 5% advanced dividend tax applies to non-distributed taxable profits at year-end
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is limited (in force: Mexico, South Korea, Singapore, France, Portugal, UAE, Qatar, United Kingdom, Barbados). Protocol: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the counterpart tax authority stating treaty residence; (ii) submit the DTA relief application via the DGI international tax window, attaching the TRC, audited financial statements, power of attorney, and a beneficial-ownership declaration; (iii) obtain the DGI authorization before applying reduced rates; the withholding agent may apply the treaty rate prospectively only after that authorization; otherwise the statutory 10% / 12.5% rate is applied and recovery is via a refund claim against DGI
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 12.5% on royalties for trademarks, patents, copyrights, and know-how paid to non-residents for exploitation in Panama; 12.5% on interest paid to non-residents, with an exemption for interest paid to Panama-licensed banks and financial institutions; DTA-reduced rates generally 5%–10% for royalties and 5%–10% for interest, subject to the protocol above. For the GDP pharma freight scope, cross-border platform/software license fees and intercompany financing must be segregated to avoid the 12.5% gross-basis WHT

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama Balboas (PAB) — pegged 1:1 with USD. Threshold: taxpayers whose annual gross income exceeds USD 5,000,000 or whose cross-border related-party transactions exceed USD 5,000,000 must file Form 21 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) and a sworn transfer-pricing technical report (Informe Pericial) prepared by an independent expert registered with the DGI. PIFs with foreign-source-only income fall below the threshold and bear no TP documentation duty unless they elect to file Form 31 or engage in Panama-source intercompany transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute applicable to all entities; substance is evaluated through (i) the territorial-source test for CIT, (ii) the SEM regime requiring a physical office and at least 3 resident employees within 12 months, and (iii) DTA/EOIR substance expectations for treaty access. A PIF acting as a passive holding vehicle for foreign GDP freight assets satisfies the minimum substance threshold if it maintains: a Registered Agent in Panama, complete accounting records lodged in Panama, an assets register, and minutes of the Foundation Council; mere brass-plate PIFs relying on DTAs to shift freight income face re-characterization as sham entities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful misclassification of Panama-source GDP freight and cold-chain storage income as foreign-source revenue; falsification of the territoriality schedule; failure to file Form 31 while physically performing logistics services in Panama; use of a PIF to shield taxable Panamanian commercial activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Código Penal Art. 288: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; fine of 5 to 10 times the evaded tax; confiscation of assets and instruments; administrative addition of 50% surcharge plus monthly interest of 1.5% on the omitted tax; loss of deduction and credit rights
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Councillors, directors, and the resident agent who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax and fines; during the fiscal-criminal process the court may impose a travel ban (impedimento de salida) and civil attachment on personal assets; conviction results in concurrent imprisonment for the legal representatives

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Beneficial Ownership Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a pure shell to avoid DTA limitations in the country of the ultimate beneficiary; failing to register the beneficial owner in the DGI's Beneficial Ownership File (Law 254 of 2021); maintaining fictitious GDP freight documentation; making asset contributions with intent to defraud foreign tax creditors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law 254 of up to USD 50,000 for incomplete or inaccurate beneficial-ownership filings; cancellation or suspension of the Registered Agent's license; the foundation's legal standing is suspended, accounts are frozen, and automatic exchange of information is triggered in favor of the foreign tax authority
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the foundation's statutory shield: contributions made in fraud of creditors are voidable via the acción pauliana; the Foundation Council and settlor are personally liable to creditors for the repatriated value; directors may face travel bans and civil restitution orders from Panamanian courts; criminal liability for false declarations to the DGI beneficial-ownership registry

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violations (Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 2019)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting GDP pharma freight payments from sanctioned or politically exposed counterparties without enhanced due diligence; processing Swift Wire or Direct ACH transactions that are the proceeds of predicate offenses; failing to file a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) within 5 business days; failure to maintain a risk-based AML manual for the freight activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 or twice the benefit obtained, whichever is higher, per infraction; suspension or revocation of the GDP freight operating license; the PIF's assets may be subject to forfeiture proceedings before the Public Ministry
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal prosecution of the compliance officer and Foundation Council members for money laundering under Código Penal Arts. 254–255: imprisonment of 3 to 10 years; freezing of personal bank accounts; travel bans and posting of a pecuniary bond; directors who execute or benefit from laundering transactions face extended terms and are barred from holding office in any Panamanian regulated entity

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border related-party transactions of the freight group exceeding USD 5,000,000 without filing Form 21 or without submitting the Informe Pericial; charging disproportionately high or low intercompany freight commissions; failing to apply the arm's length standard to the PIF's payments to or from affiliated GDP logistics companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed fine of USD 10,000 for each unfiled obligation (Form 21 and the technical report); disallowance of intercompany deductions; TP adjustment to taxable income plus a 50% surcharge on the adjustment; recharacterization of the transaction and extended statute of limitations for assessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the pricing policy are jointly liable for the adjustment, surcharge, and fines; the DGI may pierce to the parent group's assets if the Panamanian entity is undercapitalized; criminal referral is possible when the TP adjustment indicates fraudulent revenue shifting, resulting in travel bans and seizure of personal property
